summary:
"Tallest building strictly after i" is a **suffix maximum** that excludes i itself. Walk from the right end,
write the running maximum into the answer **before** including the current building, then update it. One
pass, O(n), O(1) extra space.

question.md:
For each building, return the height of the tallest building **strictly after** it, or −1 for the last
building.

- **Strictly after:** the building itself doesn't count. For `[2, 2, 2]` the answer is `[2, 2, −1]`: the
  first building sees two buildings of height 2.
- **It's the maximum, not the next taller one.** `[4, 9, 2, 7, 3]` gives 9 for the first building even
  though 9 is just one step away; for building 2 (height 2) it's 7.
- **Size:** up to 10⁵, so scanning the rest of the street for every building is too slow.

**Edge cases to keep in mind**

- The last building has nothing after it: `−1`.
- "Strictly after": a building's own height never counts for itself.
- All equal heights: every answer except the last is that height.

think.md:
**Two passes, one from each side.** Many "everything except me" or "everything to my left/right" questions split
into a part that depends only on what comes **before** an index and a part that depends only on what comes **after**
it. A left-to-right pass accumulates the first part, a right-to-left pass accumulates the second, and each index
combines them in O(1). Two linear passes replace an O(n) scan per index.

**Only the right-hand pass is needed.** "Tallest building after `i`" is a running maximum taken from the right.
Walk from the end, carrying `best` = tallest building seen so far (to the right of the current one): write `best`
as the answer **before** folding in the current building. For `[4, 9, 2, 7, 3, 3, 1]`:

approaches.title: Scan the rest of the street for each building

idea.md: For each building, scan everything after it for the maximum.

build: For each building, scan to the end.

lines.text: Maximum over the buildings strictly after i; −1 stays if there are none (heights are ≥ 1, so −1 never wins otherwise).

walk.title: For each building, scan everything after it for the tallest.

limits.md: Building `i`'s scan repeats building `i + 1`'s scan plus one more element. Carrying the maximum from the right reuses it.

approaches.title: Running maximum from the right

idea.md:
Walk from right to left with `best = −1`. At each building, record `best`, then update
`best = max(best, height)`.

**Invariant.** Just before processing index `i`, `best` is the maximum of `heights[i+1 …]` (or −1 if
empty), exactly the required answer.

build: Right to left: write `best`, then fold in the height.

lines.text: Nothing has been seen yet from the right, so the tallest-so-far is −1 (the answer for the last building).
Right to left, so everything after i has already been seen.
Record the tallest building strictly after i **before** including i itself.
Now include building i, for the buildings to its left.

steps.text: Building 6: answer = tallest seen so far (-1); then fold in its own height 1 → 1.
Building 5: answer = tallest seen so far (1); then fold in its own height 3 → 3.
Building 4: answer = tallest seen so far (3); then fold in its own height 3 → 3.
Building 3: answer = tallest seen so far (3); then fold in its own height 7 → 7.
Building 2: answer = tallest seen so far (7); then fold in its own height 2 → 7.
Building 1: answer = tallest seen so far (7); then fold in its own height 9 → 9.
Building 0: answer = tallest seen so far (9); then fold in its own height 4 → 9.

walk.title: Walk from the right, carrying the tallest building seen so far.

takeaways.md:
- **"Maximum to my right":** a running maximum from the right; write before you fold.
- Same pattern for minimum, sum, product to the left or right.
- **Pitfall:** updating `best` before writing it (includes the building itself).
